title: fix(mise): replace stale shims during sync
body:
## Problem

`mise-sync --apply` promises to converge tools and shims, but plain `mise reshim` only adds or refreshes known entries. Unknown stale links can survive after a package-managed Mise installation is removed, so apply reports success while `mise run check` still finds shims targeting the deleted executable. This was reproduced on both Linux and macOS during the multi-host rollout of #12.

## Solution

Run the canonical executable with upstream `reshim --force` semantics after the locked install. Mise removes the existing shim set and rebuilds it from installed tools, so stale package-manager targets cannot survive a successful sync. Update the command-contract tests and document that apply replaces the complete shim set.

## Related

- Follow-up to #12
- Amp rollout: https://ampcode.com/threads/T-019f8e04-1450-7079-af7c-f13ef33e51cf

## Verification

- `mise run test -- tests/test_mise_sync.py` — 23 passed
- `mise run verify` — 221 Python tests and 43 module tests passed; Ruff, ty, repository lint, and shell checks passed
- `mise run mise-sync -- --apply --json` — force reshim succeeded against the live standalone installation
- `mise run check -- --json` — no Mise ownership or shim findings after apply
